title: Terminology - Chapter 2
notes: Activity: Work performed within an organization; for example, setting up machines or distributing products.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Allocation: Process of assigning costs to cost objects, such as departments, products, or activities.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Cost: Monetary measure of resources sacrificed to achieve a specific objective.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Cost Object: Anything for which a measurement of costs is desired (product, service, department, etc.).
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Consumer: Person or entity that uses goods and services.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Direct Cost: Cost that can be conveniently and economically traced to a cost object.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Indirect Cost: Cost that cannot be conveniently and economically traced to a cost object.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Fixed Cost: Cost that remains unchanged in total for a given period despite wide changes in the related level of total activity or volume.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Variable Cost: Cost that changes in total in direct proportion to a change in activity or volume.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Mixed Cost: Cost that has both fixed and variable components.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Product Cost: Cost that is assigned to goods that were either purchased or manufactured for resale.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Period Cost: Cost that is expensed in the period in which it is incurred.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Prime Cost: Direct materials plus direct labor.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Conversion Cost: Direct labor plus manufacturing overhead.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Opportunity Cost: Benefit forgone when one alternative is chosen over another.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Sunk Cost: Cost already incurred that cannot be changed by any future decision.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Differential Cost: Difference in cost between two alternatives.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Incremental Cost: Additional cost incurred when one alternative is selected over another.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Relevant Cost: Cost that is pertinent to a decision because it has a bearing on the future and differs among alternatives.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Irrelevant Cost: Cost that is not pertinent to a decision.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Output: Product, service, or result of a process.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Production: Creation of goods and services.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Resource: Input required to produce goods and services.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Unit: Single, identifiable quantity of a product or service.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Total Output: Aggregate amount of goods and services produced.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Average Cost: Total cost divided by the number of units produced.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Marginal Cost: Cost of producing one additional unit of output.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Overhead: All production costs other than direct materials and direct labor.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Traceability: Ability to directly relate a cost to a cost object.
Chapter 2 Key Terms.pdf
Utilization: Extent to which a resource is used for its intended purpose.
